transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-05-09 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sam (Redwood SE), Mark Reynolds (Catalyst InfoSec), Tara Singh (Legal), Luis Gomez (Procurement), Anika Patel (Cloud)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough): Walked through SIG questionnaire items; flagged SOC 2 and encryption evidence requests; agreed to send reports and mapping spreadsheet.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for taking the time. Um this is Jordan from Redwood, I have Priya and Sam with me from our security team. Could we do quick intros?
[00:10] Mark Reynolds: Yep, Mark Reynolds, Head of InfoSec at Catalyst Bank. We're leading the vendor risk for this engagement.
[00:15] Tara Singh: Tara, legal counsel, I'll be looking at contract language and data residency clauses.
[00:20] Luis Gomez: Luis, procurement, just here to observe and track timeline.
[00:24] Anika Patel: Anika, cloud architect, will validate technical controls and KMS integration.
[00:29] Priya Nair: Hi all, Priya SE, I'll walk through CAIQ/SIG items and where evidence lives on our side. Quick note we might reference SOC two, sometimes transcriber writes that as 'sock two' so apologies for any typos.

[02:05] Priya Nair: Starting with overall scope: Redwood provides hosted API, dedicated pools and private deployments. For SIG we map questions across our SOC 2 report, ISO cert, policies, and evidence bucket.
[02:25] Mark Reynolds: Our main asks: strong RBAC, SSO with SAML + SCIM, audit log retention for 12 months, encryption with customer-managed keys where possible, and clear artifact paths for SOC 2 and pen testing. Also data residency — we need EU region only for some products.
[02:45] Jordan Lee: Totally understood. On SOC 2 we have Type II current through 2024 — we'll share the report. For ISO, we maintain ISO 27001 scope for our cloud control plane, we'll include the cert.
[03:10] Tara Singh: Can you confirm who signs BAA/DPAs and where data residency is enforced in the contract? Sometimes the answers are buried.
[03:22] Jordan Lee: Yes, contract team signs DPAs, and we can add clauses for region restrictions and addendum for private deployments. We'll follow up with redlined language.

[04:40] Priya Nair: On authentication: we support SAML SSO for user access and SCIM for provisioning. For RBAC we have org-level roles and token-level scopes, plus support for enterprise SSO flows via SAML with JIT provisioning. There was a previous note about SCIM not fully syncing groups in older versions — that's been fixed in our current release, but evidence will show the updated logs.
[05:20] Mark Reynolds: Do you support session timeouts and MFA enforcement?
[05:26] Priya Nair: Yes, session timeout configurable, MFA via SAML IdP policy is supported. We can provide screenshots of console settings and a sample SAML metadata file.

[07:00] Sam Ortiz: For audit logs, we retain agent and admin activity logs for 12 months by default in hosted, and for Dedicated or Private we can configure longer retention. Logs include API request traces, admin changes, and model invocation metadata — note: model token streams are not retained in full by default, only metadata unless configured.
[07:40] Anika Patel: We need to confirm what "model invocation metadata" contains — does it include full prompts or redacted?
[07:50] Sam Ortiz: Good question. By default we redact user-submitted content from long term storage; we retain metadata such as request IDs, token counts, latency, and status codes. For customers that require full content retention for debugging, we'd need explicit contractual terms. We'll add that note into the mapping.

[09:30] Priya Nair: Encryption at rest: we use customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we offer platform-managed keys by default and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options for higher tiers. Evidence: KMS architecture doc, key rotation policy, and a sample KMS access policy.
[10:05] Anika Patel: Which KMS providers are supported?
[10:08] Priya Nair: We support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP KMS for Private/DED deployments. For hosted we currently support AWS KMS BYOK; Azure and GCP are on roadmap — we'll flag timelines.

[11:30] Mark Reynolds: Data residency — how do you lock data to EU region? Is that at ingestion, storage, or processing?
[11:40] Jordan Lee: We can pin requests to specific regions via our routing policy. For hosted customers, we have regional endpoints and data-at-rest is stored in the selected region. For Dedicated and Private, obviously you control region and networking. We'll provide network diagrams and a region data-flow doc.
[12:10] Tara Singh: For CAIQ answers around encryption, access controls and monitoring, we'll need supporting artifacts — not just yes/no.
[12:17] Priya Nair: Absolutely. For each SIG/CAIQ we map the answer to: policy doc, system config screenshot, and evidence file (SOC 2 section or cert). We'll share that mapping spreadsheet after the call.

[14:00] Luis Gomez: On timelines, procurement needs the completed SIG and SOC 2 by next week to move to sales approval. Is that feasible?
[14:08] Jordan Lee: We can share the SOC 2 report and pen test by 2025-05-12, and Priya will share the CAIQ mapping by 2025-05-13. Full completed spreadsheet with evidence links might take a little longer but we'll prioritize high-risk items.

[16:30] Priya Nair: A few SIG-specific gotchas: some CAIQ questions ask for KMS key access logs — we can provide KMS audit trails for keys we manage, for BYOK you may need to pull from your KMS. Also some questions reference "real time alerting" — we have alerts integrated with webhooks and SIEM; we can provide an example rule set.

[18:45] Mark Reynolds: Regarding penetration testing, do you allow us to see scope and remediation timelines?
[18:53] Jordan Lee: Yes, we have a summarized pentest report and remediation tracker — we can share the redacted report and our remediation timeline doc.

[21:00] Anika Patel: For Private deployment, what's the lift? We're trying to see if we can host in our Azure tenancy with our own KMS.
[21:10] Sam Ortiz: For on-prem/private we provide an installer and control plane that can be run inside your VPC or peered network. You'd manage KMS and network egress rules. We'll coordinate SRE/SE for a deeper runbook in follow up.

[25:00] Tara Singh: Contract question: will Redwood accept contractual language that requires EU data to never be copied outside region? Some vendors won't sign that.
[25:12] Jordan Lee: We can accept region-locking clauses for certain product lines and workloads; we will put that to legal and provide redline examples. For hosted there's sometimes operational complexity but we can confirm on next call.

[28:30] Priya Nair: Quick note on transcription: sometimes product names get munged (e.g., KV cache as K-V cash), and the CAIQ mapping spreadsheet will be the source of truth.

[30:00] Jordan Lee: Ok let's go through a short sample question: Q1: "Do you encrypt data at rest?" Answer: "Yes — AES-256 at rest, customer-managed keys available via KMS for Dedicated/Private. Evidence: KMS architecture diagram, SOC 2 CC6 section, key rotation policy."
[31:10] Mark Reynolds: Q2: "How long are admin audit logs retained?"
[31:14] Sam Ortiz: "12 months default for hosted; configurable for Dedicated/Private — evidence: logging retention policy and sample log export."

[33:00] Priya Nair: For identity proofing: we use SAML SSO and SCIM, and we can provide a SAML metadata file and provisioning logs. For role separation, we have admin vs org vs developer roles. Evidence will be role matrix and sample role bindings.

[36:40] Mark Reynolds: One more on incident response: can you share your IR runbook summary and last tabletop results?
[36:48] Jordan Lee: We can share an IR summary doc and the SOC 2 coverage shows IR controls; tabletop details are somewhat internal but we can provide high-level outcomes and remediation actions.

[40:20] Tara Singh: On legal hold and eDiscovery — if regulator requests logs, what's the process?
[40:27] Priya Nair: We have playbooks for legal requests; for hosted customers we coordinate with our security and legal teams. We'll provide the legal request playbook redacted.

[42:50] Jordan Lee: Recap: Jordan will upload SOC 2 + pen test (due 5/12), Priya will share CAIQ mapping + evidence links (due 5/13), Sam to prepare a deeper technical runbook for Private deploy and KMS (target 5/19). We will schedule follow-up encryption/KMS deep dive.

[46:00] Mark Reynolds: Thanks, appreciate the clarity. We'll review and circle back with any follow-ups.
[46:12] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and links after this meeting. Bye.

End of transcript. Some small transcription errors likely (names/ acronyms).
